summary.summary: This is the covering report introducing the Chief Finance Officer's Treasury Management 2025/26 Annual Report, which itself will go to full Council on 16 July 2026 as Annex 1; that annex (with the outturn figures, borrowing, investment maturity and prudential-indicator tables) was not included in the packet supplied to this reading, so no borrowing, CFR or investment figures could be grounded from what was read. What the covering report does confirm is two proposed amendments to the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy: excluding Hart and Rushmoor councils from individual counterparty limits for local-authority loans, and raising the Prudential Limit for 'Long-Term Principal Investments to Mature' in 2027/28 and 2028/29. Both changes loosen existing limits rather than tighten them, which is worth a lender's attention even though the covering report gives no revised limit figures.

signals.headline: Council proposes raising the Prudential Limit for 'Long-Term Principal Investments to Mature' in 2027/28 and 2028/29, and excluding Hart and Rushmoor from individual counterparty limits, rather than tightening either
signals.why: Raising a prudential limit and loosening a counterparty concentration limit both increase the amount of exposure the council permits itself, rather than reducing risk.

news_drafts.headline: Basingstoke and Deane draft budget balances 2027/28 and 2028/29, with a £1.57m gap in 2029/30
news_drafts.lead:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's draft medium term financial strategy (MTFS) shows a balanced budget for 2027/28 and 2028/29, according to the budget report before Cabinet on 10 November 2026. For 2029/30 it shows a gap of £1.57m.

The report sets out the position after Cabinet's proposals. The 2029/30 figure is lower than the £1.93m gap in the MTFS update presented to Council in February 2026. In the report's words: "This is a reduction from the £1.93M budget gap contained in the MTFS update presented to Council in February 2026."

The report states that the 2029/30 gap will need to be addressed for the council to set a balanced budget in that year.

news_drafts.headline: Basingstoke and Deane's auditor expects a qualified opinion, with its scope still to be decided
news_drafts.lead:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's external auditor, which carries out the independent check on its accounts, expects to give a qualified audit opinion, meaning it could not fully sign off the accounts. It has not yet decided which areas the qualification will cover. The position is set out in an appendix to the Audit and Accounts Committee papers for its meeting on 28 September.

The auditor is still rebuilding its assurance over the council's reserves, the money it has put aside, after earlier years in which it gave no opinion at all. Four balances are marked "to be confirmed" rather than as fully or partly assured: the General Fund Balance, the Revaluation Reserve, the Capital Adjustment Account and the Pooled Investments Fund.

The paper says: "Although a qualification is anticipated, the basis and scope of that qualification will be determined upon completion of the remaining audit procedures." The rebuilding work was commissioned under the audit recovery programme of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

findings.headline: Bank Rate increased by 0.25% to 4.00% in November, against an MTFS assumption of a fall to 3.25% by end-2026
findings.detail: The Medium-Term Financial Strategy had assumed the base rate would fall to 3.25% by the end of 2026. The paper reports that in November the Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate instead. The paper also notes that higher inflation and an increase in base rate are expected this financial year.
findings.matters: A change of rate direction against the MTFS assumption affects the treasury income forecast, and finance officers at other councils will be checking the same assumption.
findings.figures: Bank Rate 3.75% at start of year; MTFS assumption 3.25% by end-2026; 0.25% increase to 4.00%; CPI 3.5% in September
findings.quote: increased the Bank Rate (base rate) by 0.25% to 4.00%

findings.headline: External fund valuations at £22.37M on 30 September 2026 against a £25.00M initial cost
findings.detail: The paper reports a reduction of £2.63M against cost, with the Royal London Short Dated Credit Fund and CCLA Local Authorities Property Fund both lower in-year. It states that the statutory IFRS 9 override means no impact on the income and expenditure account from valuation changes until at least 2029/30.
findings.matters: A finance director can see the unrealised loss on pooled funds and the period over which the statutory override defers its revenue impact, which bears on the timing of any loss.
findings.figures: £22.37M valuation at 30 September 2026; £25.00M initial cost; £2.63M reduction against cost; £0.27M decrease in 2026/27; override to 1 April 2029
findings.quote: was £22.37M compared to an initial cost of £25.00M

findings.headline: Council removed counterparty limits for Rushmoor and Hart councils, with £20.00M held in Rushmoor Borough Council loans
findings.detail: Council approved on 16 July 2026 the removal of counterparty limits for Rushmoor and Hart councils, citing the expectation of Local Government Reorganisation. Appendix 1 shows two Rushmoor Borough Council loans totalling £20.00M, one maturing 02/12/2026 at 4.15% and one maturing 03/04/2028 at 4.50%.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance officers at other councils facing reorganisation will see that a council has relaxed its counterparty limits for councils in that position, and that its own exposure to one of them is now £20.00M.
findings.figures: £20.00M across two Rushmoor Borough Council loans; £10.00M at 4.15% maturing 02/12/2026; £10.00M at 4.50% maturing 03/04/2028
findings.quote: The removal of counterparty limits for Rushmoor and Hart councils due to the expectation of LGR was approved by Council on 16 July 2026.

findings.headline: Long-term loan income forecast at £0.78M for 2026/27 against a £0.43M budget, after a new loan made in 2025/26
findings.detail: The paper says the return on long-term loans, which are usually made to other local authorities at fixed rates, has been enhanced by a loan made after the 2025/26 budget was set. Long-term loan income is the largest single variance in the income table after bond funds and liquidity cash.
findings.matters: It shows the council acting as a lender to other local authorities, and a finance director at another council can see the income that a fixed-rate loan to a peer produced.
findings.figures: £0.78M forecast long-term loan income; £0.43M budget; £0.35M variance; £20.00M long-term loans held
findings.quote: The return from these investments has been enhanced by a new loan made after this year’s budget was set in 2025/26.

findings.headline: Forecast overall treasury investment return of 4.22% for 2026/27 against a 3.80% budget estimate
findings.detail: The paper expects the average return across treasury investments to exceed budget, with bond funds, short-term investments and liquidity cash forecast above their budget returns. Average investment balance is now expected to be £123.64M against an original estimate of £116.16M.
findings.matters: The gap between the forecast return and the budget estimate is the main driver of the income uplift, so a peer council can compare its own return assumptions against this figure.
findings.figures: 4.22% forecast return; 3.80% budget estimate; +0.42 variance; £123.64M expected average balance; £116.16M original estimate
findings.quote: The overall return on treasury management investments is forecast to be 4.22% compared to the budget estimate of 3.80%.

daily_post.headline: Council has an obligation to provide 250 car parking spaces for the AA at Basing View, which must be relocated after Fanum House demolition
